Senses.Explanation: Literally, “the one phrase before sound.” Across 89 occurrences in 55 allowlisted texts, it is chiefly a public-interview question and case-commentary heading, not a term the corpus leaves outside speech. Asked “what is the phrase before sound?” one master answers with the vocalization “un” (吽), and another says, “it is just like not saying” (恰似不道). Huanglian directly answers, “before sound there is no phrase; after the sound, bring your question” (聲前無句，聲後問將來). Later addresses make contrary predicates within the same public record: one says “everyone originally has” the phrase, while the Blue Cliff Record says “the thousand sages do not transmit” it. These are attested answers and claims, not grounds for choosing an ineffable reading. Zen bends the temporal phrase into a recurrent interview prompt whose answers may themselves be spoken sounds; this entry preserves that observable deployment and the corpus’s own disagreement.
Senses.Note: The phrase as question, heading, and quoted line denotes the same interview expression. Different answers—including sound, refusal, possession, and denial—are readings or responses, not different things and therefore not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是聲前一句。師曰吽。曰轉後如何。師曰。是什麼。
問如何是聲前一句。師曰。恰似不道。
僧問黃連和尚：如何是聲前一句？連云：聲前無句，聲後問將來。
聲前一句，人人本具，放過一著，落在第二，若不放過，打出骨髓。
聲前一句。千聖不傳。未曾親覲。如隔大千。

Senses.Explanation: The paired sensory objects of ear and eye: sound (聲) and visible form or color (色). Chan records do more than repeat the pair abstractly. Yongjia's exchange explicitly assigns them to the faculties — 'when eyes and ears meet sound and form' (眼耳緣聲色時) — and asks what is the substance of sound and form. Dahui makes the pair demonstrable during a public address: he raises the whisk and says, 'this is form,' strikes the Chan seat and says, 'this is sound' (這箇是色／這箇是聲). Another record gives ordinary audible examples: wind in pine trees, frogs, and crows are all sound, while saying that what one discriminates is sound and form. The corpus also predicates 'pass through all sound and form without obstruction' (透一切聲色，無有滯礙) and draws its own distinction between function 'together with sound and form' and 'the affairs of sound and form' (用同聲色而不是聲色之事). The Zen deviation is this repeated use as a named field of public testing and concrete demonstration; the graphs still denote what is heard and seen.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count for the unsplit string: 2,214 hits in 311 texts. Primary family check: 'visible form/color' (色), 'sound' (聲), 'seeing and hearing' (見聞), 'sound, form, and language' (聲色言語), and 'sound, form, and names' (聲色名字). The ordinary 'sensual attractions' and the idiom 'without changing voice or expression' refer to different things and are split below under depth-gate item 8.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲識大道真體。不離聲色言語。舉起拂子云。這箇是色。擊禪床云。這箇是聲。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Concrete public demonstration: raised whisk = form; struck Chan seat = sound.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。眼耳緣聲色時。為復抗行。為有回互。澤曰。抗互且置。汝指何法為聲色之體乎。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The exchange explicitly pairs eyes and ears with form and sound and asks what counts as their substance.

Occurrences.Kwic: 對一切境，心無靜亂，不攝不散，透一切聲色，無有滯礙，名為道人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Predicate deployment: 'pass through all sound and form without obstruction' appears in a passage that says this is called a person of the Way.

Occurrences.Kwic: 記持得底是名字，揀辨得底是聲色。若不是聲色名字，汝又作麼生記持揀辨？風吹松樹也是聲，蝦蟇老鵶叫也是聲
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Text-drawn relation between names and sound/form, followed by concrete sound examples: wind in pines, frogs, and crows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 體絕見聞而不離見聞之緣，用同聲色而不是聲色之事
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The text itself contrasts functioning together with sound/form against being an affair of sound/form.

Senses.Explanation: A distinct ordinary referent in biographical and admonitory prose: worldly sensual attractions or entertainments, commonly coordinated with wealth, status, and profit. Zhao Bian's biography says that after forty he 'cast off sensual attractions' (擯去聲色) and turned his attention to the records of the school. Another record warns against simultaneously pursuing achievement, receiving wealth and honor, 'indulging in sensual attractions' (耽聲色), and attending to worldly affairs. This is not the eye-and-ear field concretely demonstrated by a whisk and struck seat, so it remains a separate sense.
Senses.Note: The phrase 'cast off sensual attractions' (擯去聲色) occurs in nine allowlist texts, chiefly recensions of the same Zhao Bian biography; 'indulge in sensual attractions' (耽聲色) supplies a structurally independent witness. No distinctively Chan lexical bend was found for this ordinary sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 清獻公趙抃居士字悅道，衢州西安人。年四十餘，擯去聲色，系心宗教。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Biographical use: Zhao Bian casts off sensual attractions after forty.

Occurrences.Kwic: 非一面作功名、受富貴、耽聲色、料理世情，一面又去學可以了得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sensual attractions coordinated with achievement, wealth and honor, and management of worldly affairs.

Senses.Explanation: The two outward signs in the fixed phrase 'without changing voice or expression' (不動聲色): voice or tone (聲) and facial look or demeanor (色). A record praises Huanglong's forty years presiding over a community as 'holding the seat of the community without changing voice or expression' (坐鎮道場，不動聲色); a public interview likewise asks whether something can be discerned 'without changing voice or expression.' This idiomatic human demeanor is a different referent from sounds and visible objects in the sensory field.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count for 'without changing voice or expression' (不動聲色): 20 hits in 15 texts. Kept separate because a person's voice and expression and the field of heard and seen objects cannot share one precise English gloss.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南禪師住黃龍四十年，坐鎮道場，不動聲色。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Biographical appraisal: forty years presiding at Huanglong without changing voice or expression.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「打鼓弄琵琶，相逢兩作家，秪如不動聲色還辯得麼？」師云：「三千里外少知音。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Public interview use of the fixed idiom: can it still be discerned without changing voice or expression?

Senses.Explanation: Literally a monk (僧) in a patched robe (衲), a “patch-robed monk,” attested 8,708 times in 376 allowlisted texts. The term names the Chan monk as a participant addressed, questioned, or assessed in the records. Asked “what is a patch-robed monk?” (如何是衲僧), one teacher answers, “investigating, seeking, and visiting the Way” (參尋訪道). Another exchange asks for “the patch-robed monk's own affair” (衲僧分上事) and answers, “when you want to walk, walk; when you want to sit, sit” (要行即行，要坐即坐). The corpus also asks directly about “the patch-robed monk's eye” (衲僧眼) and “the patch-robed monk's place of conduct” (衲僧行履處). It speaks institutionally of what can be used “under the patch-robed monk's gate” (衲僧門下), and appraises an assembly as lacking anyone with “the air of a patch-robed monk” (衲僧氣息). The Chan deviation lies in this public standard: the robe-word names the person expected to answer within the encounter record, while the compounds test that person's eye, conduct, handle, own affair, and house. These are attested compound deployments, not claims about an inner state.
Senses.Note: The records use the same human-role noun individually, collectively, and possessively. Yuanwu calls raising one and understanding three “ordinary tea and rice for the household of patch-robed monks” (衲僧家尋常茶飯), and elsewhere calls activity that ferries beings “the patch-robed monk's own affair” (衲僧家本分事). Eye, gate, conduct, air, household, own portion, and handle compounds do not denote a second kind of monk. Compare monk (僧), master or preceptor (和尚), this old monk (老僧), the household of patch-robed monks (衲僧家), and patched robe (衲衣).

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是衲僧。師曰。參尋訪道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Under the heading for Yun'gaishan Zhiyuan: "What is a patch-robed monk?" The teacher says, "investigating, seeking, and visiting the Way." The roster has no safe exact link for the heading name.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰。如何是衲僧分上事。師曰。要行即行。要坐即坐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Under the same heading: "What is the patch-robed monk's own affair?" The teacher answers, "when you want to walk, walk; when you want to sit, sit."

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉一明三。目機銖兩。是衲僧家尋常茶飯。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Instruction introducing a Blue Cliff case: "raise one, understand three; assess the pivot by the slightest weight—this is ordinary tea and rice for the household of patch-robed monks." The structural heading is not a safe speaker attribution.

Occurrences.Kwic: 梯航三有津濟四生。是衲僧家本分事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu says, "serve as ladder and boat across the three modes of existence and ferry the four kinds of birth: this is the patch-robed monk's own affair."

Occurrences.Kwic: 句能剗意意能剗句。意句交馳衲僧巴鼻。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu says, "sentences can strip intent and intent can strip sentences; intent and sentences racing across one another are the patch-robed monk's handle."

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是衲僧眼師云朝看東南暮看西北
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public interview asks, “what is the patch-robed monk's eye?” (如何是衲僧眼). The teacher answers, “in the morning look southeast; in the evening look northwest” (朝看東南暮看西北).

Occurrences.Kwic: 若論衲僧門下，一點也用不得。作麼生是衲僧門下事？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The speaker says that, “under the patch-robed monk's gate” (衲僧門下), not one bit of the preceding material can be used, then asks, “what is the affair under the patch-robed monk's gate?” (作麼生是衲僧門下事).

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是衲僧行履處。師曰。頭上喫棒。口裏喃喃。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Asked “what is the patch-robed monk's place of conduct?” (如何是衲僧行履處), the teacher answers, “taking a staff-blow on the head, muttering in the mouth” (頭上喫棒，口裏喃喃).

Occurrences.Kwic: 眾中更無一人有衲僧氣息。諸人還見世尊以手摩胸麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The speaker says, “in the assembly there is not even one person with the air of a patch-robed monk” (眾中更無一人有衲僧氣息), then asks whether they saw the World-Honored One rub his chest with his hand.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, a 'patched-robed person': 'patched robe' (衲) plus the person-noun (子). The term occurs 2,174 times in 317 allowed texts and names the monks who travel among, gather around, question, and are addressed by Chan teachers. A later small assembly gives the only direct naming formula found: 'all of you wear hats and waist-packs and are called patch-robed monks; the name and the reality ought to match' (箇箇都是頂笠腰包，名為衲子，要當名實相稱). In Nanquan's recorded exchange with Zhaozhou, Nanquan says, 'dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish; patch-robed monks are hard to fool' (龍蛇易辨衲子難謾). A biography says that after a monastery was built, 'patch-robed monks hastened there like clouds' (衲子雲趨). Ciming speaks of sitting on a rock and at times discussing the profound with 'patch-robed monks from the five lakes' (與五湖衲子時話玄微); the longer form 'five-lakes patch-robed monks' (五湖衲子) occurs 57 times. Qingchu praises a traveller twice: 'Fine patch-robed monk! Fine patch-robed monk!' (衲子俊哉。衲子俊哉). A biography of Shending Yin describes him as 'extraordinary even among patch-robed monks; none dared enter his gate' (衲子非人類精奇。無敢登其門者). The noun therefore functions as singular praise, plural group-name, travelling population, and the object of tests and appraisals.
Senses.Note: No other required direct-definition formula was found; three late 'what is a patch-robed monk' questions give case-specific replies. The direct naming line, robe morphology, and broad early corpus deployment support the plain target without adding an imported religious category.

Occurrences.Kwic: 你諸人，箇箇都是頂笠腰包，名為衲子，要當名實相稱
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Pin Jixiang's record, small assembly. The speaker says those before him wear hats and waist-packs and are called patch-robed monks, adding that name and reality should match. No exact roster link is available.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。龍蛇易辨衲子難謾
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Nanquan section. After Zhaozhou catches Nanquan's staff, Nanquan says patch-robed monks are harder to fool than dragons and snakes are to distinguish.

Occurrences.Kwic: 相與建寺。衲子雲趨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium, Longhu Puwen biography: people built a monastery together and patch-robed monks hastened there like clouds. Narrative biography remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 與五湖衲子時話玄微。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp, Ciming's biography: he at times discussed the profound with patch-robed monks from the five lakes. The broad lineage head and biographical voice make a null key safer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衲子俊哉。衲子俊哉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium, Qingchu and Deshan encounter. Qingchu praises the traveller twice, 'Fine patch-robed monk!' The two-person exchange remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衲子非人類精奇。無敢登其門者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp, Shending Yin biography: he was extraordinary among patch-robed monks, and none dared enter his gate. Narrative appraisal remains unkeyed.
